questions.q:
A person's wound was exposed to some bacteria and then bacteria growth started to happen at the same place. The wound was later treated with some antibacterial medicine and the rate of bacterial decay (r) was found to be proportional with the square of the existing number of bacteria at any instance. Which of the following set of graphs correctly represents the 'before' and 'after' situation of the application of the medicine?
[Given : $\mathrm{N}=$ No. of bacteria, $\mathrm{t}=$ time, bacterial growth follows $I^{\text {st }}$ order kinetics.]
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.solution:
*Before applying medicine
$\frac{\mathrm{dA}}{\mathrm{dt}}=\mathrm{K}[\mathrm{A}]$ (First order growth) (Rate law)
$\frac{\mathrm{A}}{\mathrm{~A}_0}=\frac{\mathrm{N}}{\mathrm{~N}_0}=\mathrme^{\mathrm{Kt}}$
*After applying medicine

$\mathrm{r}=-\frac{\mathrm{dA}}{\mathrm{dt}}=\mathrm{K}[\mathrm{A}]^2 \quad$ (Rate law)
$y=\mathrm{Kx}^2$ Parabola

questions.q:
A student has studied the decomposition of a gas $A{B}_{3}$~at $25 ° C$. He obtained the following data

$p ( mmHg )$ $50$ $100$ $200$ $400$
Relative~$t\dfrac{1}{2} \left(s\right)$ $4$ $2$ $1$ $0 . 5

The order of the reaction is

$
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.solution:
By observing the data given, by doubling the pressure, half-life is reduced to half. This result is following second order kinetics. Mathematically it can be proved as follows,

The half-life and initial pressure of& $n^{th}$~order reaction can be related as follows,

$t\dfrac{1}{2} ∝ \left({P}_{o}\right)1 - n$

$\dfrac{\left({t}_{\dfrac{1}{2}}\right)1}{\left(t\dfrac{1}{2}\right)2} = {{P}_{0}}_{1}^{1 - n}{{P}_{0}}_{2}^{1 - n}$

$⇒ \left(\dfrac{4}{2}\right) = \left(\dfrac{50}{100}\right)1 - n$

$⇒ 2 = \left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)1 - n$

$⇒ 2 = \left(2\right)n - 1$

$⇒ n - 1 = 1$

$⇒ n = 2$

Hence, the order of the reaction is second order.

questions.q: A bacterial infection in an internal wound grows as $N^{'}\left(t\right) = {N}_{0}exp ⁡ ( t )$ , where the time $t$ is in hours. A dose of antibiotic, taken orally, needs 1 hour to reach the wound. Once it reaches there, the bacterial population goes down as $\dfrac{dN}{dt} = - 5N^{2}$ . What will be the plot of $\dfrac{{N}_{0}}{N}$ vs $t$ after $1$ hour?
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.solution:
From 0 to 1 hour, $N^{'} = {N}_{0}e^{t}$
From 1 hour onwards $\dfrac{dN}{dt} = - 5N^{2}$
So at $t = 1$ hour, $N^{'} = e{N}_{0}$
$\dfrac{dN}{dt} = - 5N^{2}$
${∫}_{e{N}_{0}}^{N}N^{- 2}dN = - 5{∫}_{1}^{t}dt$
$\dfrac{1}{N} - \dfrac{1}{e{N}_{0}} = 5 \left(t - 1\right)$
\dfrac{{N}_{0}}{N} - \dfrac{1}{e} =$5{N}_{0} ( t - 1 )$
\dfrac{{N}_{0}}{N} =$5{N}_{0} ( t - 1 ) + $\dfrac{1}{e}
\dfrac{{N}_{0}}{N} =$5{N}_{0}t + \left(\dfrac{1}{e} -5{N}_{0}\right)$
Which is following $y = mx + C$

\left[$B\right] = \dfrac{{k}_{1}\left[A\right]}{{k}_{2}}

questions.q:
$\begin{cases}\left[A\right] & \to & \left[B\right] \\ Reactant & & Product\end{cases}$

If formation of compound \left[B\right]$~follows the first order of kinetics and after $70$ minutes the concentration of \left[A\right]$ was found to be half of its initial concentration. Then the rate constant of the reaction is $x \times {10}^{- 6}s^{- 1}$. The value of $x$& is____
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.solution:
$\begin{cases}\left[A\right] & \to & \left[B\right] \\ Reactant & & Product\end{cases}$

Since the reaction follows the first order~kinetics and after $70$ minutes the concentration of \left[A\right]$ was found to be half of its initial concentration. That means 70 minutes is the half life time for the reaction. And we know that for a first order reaction half life time is given as.

$t\dfrac{1}{2} = \dfrac{0 . 693}{K}K = \dfrac{0 . 693}{t\dfrac{1}{2}} = \dfrac{0 . 693}{70 \times 60sec .}$

$= \dfrac{6930}{7 \times 6} \times {10}^{- 6}\sec^{- 1} = 165 \times {10}^{- 6}\sec^{- 1}So, x = 165$

$

$log \left(\dfrac{k2}{k1}\right) = \dfrac{Ea}{2 .303 R}\left[\dfrac{1}{T1} - \dfrac{1}{T2}\right]

$log \left(3 .555\right) = \dfrac{Ea}{2 .303 R}\left[\dfrac{1}{303} - \dfrac{1}{313}\right]$

$1 .268 \times 8 .314 \times 303 = 10Ea$
